purpose: Labelled corpus for the CodeTrace evaluation. Every case states, before the analysis is run, what the tool is expected to report. The labels are authored by hand from the source code; the harness in run_evaluation.py compares them with the actual output. Metrics computed from this file describe this corpus only.
matching: A reported finding matches an expectation when the rule id, the category and the normalised text of the sink statement all agree. Line numbers are recorded for readability and are checked as well, but they are not the identity of a finding.

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.rationale: input() is concatenated into a command and passed to system() through a helper function.

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.rationale: A user-controlled string is interpolated into a query executed by sql_exec().

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.rationale: A command-line argument is appended to a directory prefix and read as a file.

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.rationale: An environment variable is used directly as a format string.

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.rationale: Taint survives two copies before reaching the sink.

cases.label: safe
cases.rationale: The command is a literal; no untrusted data flows into it.

cases.label: safe
cases.rationale: The untrusted value is only printed; a different value reaches the sink. This is the classic false-positive trap.

cases.label: safe
cases.rationale: The tainted value is overwritten with a constant before the sink.

cases.label: safe
cases.rationale: The sink is inside a branch whose condition is the literal 0, so it cannot execute.

cases.label: sanitized
cases.rationale: shell_escape is declared for the command context and removes command taint.

cases.label: sanitized
cases.rationale: sql_escape is declared for the SQL context and removes SQL taint.

cases.label: sanitized
cases.rationale: to_int converts the value to a number; the text representation that carried the taint is gone.

cases.label: sanitized
cases.rationale: The value reaches the sink only behind a declared validator guard.

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.rationale: Taint crosses a function boundary through the return value.

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.rationale: Taint crosses two call boundaries: through an argument, a parameter and a return value.

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.rationale: A recursive helper returns its argument. Recursion is handled with a bounded summary fixpoint, so the flow is reported with certainty 'approximate' rather than 'confirmed'.

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.rationale: sql_escape is declared for the SQL context only; it must not clear command taint, and the raw value still reaches sql_exec.

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.rationale: An unmodelled function must not be assumed to sanitise its argument.

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.rationale: The engine does not track array elements individually, so an element write taints the array; documented and reported.

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.rationale: The flow is reported as structurally possible, with the guarding condition recorded and not evaluated.

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.rationale: Two different sources reach two different sinks.

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.rationale: Taint is carried through a loop-carried assignment inside a while body.

cases.label: unsupported
cases.rationale: switch is not part of the analysed subset; the file must produce explicit diagnostics (unsupported keyword and operator) instead of being analysed as if switch were safe. Recovery limits the error cascade, so SYN011 (too many errors) is deliberately not expected.

cases.label: unsupported
cases.rationale: A preprocessor directive is outside the subset and is reported.

cases.label: unsupported
cases.rationale: Pointer types are outside the subset: the declarator cannot be parsed, and the parser reports a located syntax error instead of guessing.

cases.label: syntax_error
cases.rationale: One missing semicolon must yield a located syntax error and recovery that still parses the rest of the function.

cases.label: syntax_error
cases.rationale: An unclosed brace must be reported rather than silently accepted.

cases.label: syntax_error
cases.rationale: An operator without a right operand must be reported at the failing token.

cases.label: custom_rule
cases.rationale: With the custom rule file loaded, exactly one flow is reported (the unescaped value); built-in rules add nothing because the file uses fictional APIs.
